registeredBy: Sam (owner); registered on his instruction to close the predictive econometrics gaps, before any run of this test
hypothesis: A ridge regression nowcast of quarterly real GDP growth (q/q), made 30 days after the quarter ends from up to ten predictors published by then (GDP growth in the four quarters before; the activity index growth and the OECD leading indicator change in the quarter and the one before; the change in average inflation and in the average policy rate in the quarter), with the penalty chosen in time order (first 80% of past quarters fit, last 20% scored), has a lower RMSE than the historical mean of GDP growth published by then.
knownLimits: Same release lags, countries, quarters and pass mark as gdp_nowcast v1 (the bridge equation), so the two compare like for like; policy rates are taken as known the day after the month ends.
Values are today's vintage (later revisions included): a pseudo real-time test.
Penalty grids: ridge alpha 0.01 to 1,000, lasso alpha 0.001 to 1 (20 points each, evenly spaced on a log scale), on standardised predictors, as scikit-learn's StandardScaler with Ridge or Lasso.
The euro area policy rate enters for the first euro area country in the list only (a shared rate is not repeated).
Registered together with gdp_nowcast_lasso; the Holm correction counts both.
